data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Decentralized networks are more resilient to correlated failure because organic heterogeneity in implementation stacks creates a 'biological' immunity to single-point software vulnerabilities.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services converge on a single dominant framework or cloud provider (SCR_001).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The failure trigger is a protocol-level flaw (e.g., TCP/IP or DNS) rather than an implementation-level flaw.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Unlike centralized redundancy, which typically clones a single 'golden image' (creating a uniform attack surface), decentralized services utilize diverse OS kernels, language runtimes, and configuration quirks. A specific exploit or logic bug (e.g., a buffer overflow in a specific library version) that would catastrophically fail 100% of a centralized service's redundant nodes will only affect the subset of decentralized nodes sharing that specific stack, effectively capping the maximum correlated failure at the 'Diversity Threshold' (SCR_005).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
